draft.title: The sonnet and other fixed forms
card: A fixed form is a poem built to a set pattern, such as a set number of lines or a set rhyme scheme. The pattern gives shape to the poet's idea.
Sonnet
a poem of 14 lines with a set rhyme pattern. Two well-known types are the Shakespearean sonnet and the Petrarchan sonnet, which arrange their rhymes differently.
Turn
Many sonnets have a turn, where the argument shifts, such as from a problem to a response. Where the turn falls can differ from sonnet to sonnet.
Free verse
poetry with no set pattern of rhyme or line length. The poet decides the shape of each line to suit the idea.
draft.remember: A sonnet has 14 lines, a set rhyme pattern and often a turn. Free verse has no set pattern.

opts: A 14-line poem with a set rhyme pattern
A 12-line poem with no set rhyme pattern

a.why: A sonnet has 14 lines and a set rhyme pattern. A poem with no set pattern is free verse, so the option with 14 lines but no rhyme pattern is tempting but wrong.
a.clue: Count the lines, then check for a pattern.

b.q: Priya writes a poem about her grandmother's garden. It has no rhyme scheme, and each line is a different length. Which form is it?
opts: Free verse, because it follows no set pattern
A sonnet, because it is about one subject
A sonnet, because poems about gardens are sonnets
Free verse, because it has no turn in its argument
b.why: A poem with no set rhyme or line length is free verse. A sonnet is defined by its 14 lines and rhyme pattern, not by its subject. A missing turn does not make a poem free verse, as a turn is only common in sonnets.
b.clue: Look at what the poem lacks: a set pattern.

a.best: A 14-line poem with a set rhyme pattern

b.best: Free verse, because it follows no set pattern

problems.detail: The clue 'Look at what the poem lacks: a set pattern' repeats the exact wording of the right option ('follows no set pattern'). A student could match the words without knowing the idea.

The why says 'a turn is only common in sonnets'. This can be read as 'turns occur only in sonnets', which is false. The card says many sonnets have a turn. Better wording would be 'a turn is common in sonnets but not required'.
